search_notes: PATINA (AFT-38). Joint Pfizer and Alliance Foundation Trials release on Business Wire, dated 12 Dec 2024 08:15 ET, read from a Wayback Machine copy (businesswire.com and pfizer.com return 403; the release URL carries 20241211): statistically significant PFS improvement by investigator assessment, median 44.3 vs 29.1 months, HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.58-0.94), unstratified 1-sided p=0.0074, OS immature; presented the same day at SABCS 2024 (GS2-12). Targeted Oncology coverage dated 2024-12-12 (opened) gives the same numbers and names NCT02947685. A SABCS press-programme file named PATINA_Abstract_12-11-24.pdf now returns 404 and was not read; GS2-12 is not in Crossref. Later: NEJM paper (PMID 41604639, AFT release dated 2026-01-28) HR 0.75 (0.59-0.96); registry results posted 2026-02-12. One web search, which gave the release and coverage.

DEDICATION-1 (NVALT-30), non-inferiority design. Only a pre-planned interim analysis is public: ESMO 2024 abstract 1258MO (Ann Oncol 35:S806, DOI 10.1016/j.annonc.2024.08.1315; title seen in Crossref, record created 2024-09-17, abstract page 403) and Targeted Oncology coverage dated 2024-09-14 (opened, names NCT04909684): 1-year OS 57.7% vs 55.0%, no significant difference, criteria for continued enrolment met (256 patients analysed, per a web search summary of the abstract); no non-inferiority conclusion. Not the primary analysis. The EU CTIS record 2024-516195-15-00 (fetched from the public API) gives 750 planned, recruitment end date 2026-06-25 and estimated end 2028-06-30, so a 1-year OS analysis of the full trial is not due before mid-2027. Papers of Nov 2025 and May 2026 (full text opened in Europe PMC) call the trial ongoing or its results preliminary. Nothing later in Europe PMC (number, DEDICATION-1, NVALT-30), OpenAlex, Crossref titles on low or reduced dose pembrolizumab 2024-2026, or by investigator (van den Heuvel). The ASCO 2026 LBA1510 low-dose pembrolizumab phase 3 (first author Menon, title only) is another trial. ClinicalTrials.gov record stale: status unknown, last update 2024-04-11. One web search.

LungTIME-C01. First disclosure: ASCO 2025 abstract 8516 (J Clin Oncol 43:16_suppl), which names NCT05549037: 210 patients, median PFS 13.2 vs 6.5 months, HR 0.43 (95% CI 0.31-0.60), P<0.0001, reported as a significant PFS benefit of early time-of-day dosing. Abstract text read from the Crossref record (ascopubs.org not opened); the date is that record's creation date, the issue is dated 2025-06-01, ASCO's own release date not confirmed. RESULT WITHDRAWN: the Nature Medicine paper (2026-02-02, PMID 41629425, HR 0.40, 0.29-0.55) carries an expression of concern (2026-02-19) and a retraction note (2026-06-24, Crossref); a news article of 2026-06-25 (appliedclinicaltrialsonline.com, opened) quotes the note: the editors 'no longer have confidence in the integrity of the results'. The ASCO abstract was retracted on 2026-07-07 (Crossref). The retraction notes themselves could not be opened. primary_result is therefore 'unclear'; as first reported it was 'met', and the HR cells hold the retracted figure. A commentary (Cancer Immunol Res, Aug 2026, opened) says the registered primary endpoint was changed during the trial and dates the first public disclosure to May 2025. One web search (retraction).

ATOMIC (Alliance A021502), ASCO 2025 plenary LBA1. Earliest dated source: ASCO Daily News item, Crossref record created 2025-06-01, title only read ('ATOMIC: Atezolizumab + FOLFOX Significantly Improves DFS, Reduces Recurrence Risk in Stage III dMMR Colon Cancer'; the page returns 403). Abstract LBA1 read in full from its Crossref record (created 2025-06-04, issue dated 2025-06-10), names NCT02912559: second interim analysis, 124 DFS events, 3-year DFS 86.4% vs 76.6%, HR 0.50 (95% CI 0.35-0.72), stratified log-rank p<0.0001, crossing the efficacy boundary of 0.009. Accrual was complete (712 patients, to Jan 2023), so recorded as met, not stopped_efficacy. hr_first_public_date is the date of the abstract record I read; the HR was almost certainly shown on 2025-06-01. Later: NEJM paper 2026-03-26 (PMID 41880612) HR 0.50 (0.35-0.73); registry results posted 2026-04-14. No earlier press release found: one web search returned only meeting coverage from June 2025 and publication releases of March 2026; Genentech or Roche documents were not searched.

AlloRelapseMM. Registry: terminated, 28 patients enrolled, primary completion 2025-03-14, no results posted; reason given: 'the recruitment target could not be achieved despite all efforts and the G-BA (financing party) does not consider a continuation ... to be expedient'. Primary endpoint was overall survival at 5 years after randomisation, so no primary analysis exists or is possible. Europe PMC by number and acronym: only the design paper (BMC Cancer 2025-01-27, PMID 39865222) and reviews; OpenAlex by acronym: the design paper only. No web search.

SCST-01 (TC vs BEP, ovarian sex cord-stromal tumours). Nothing found. Registry: still 'recruiting', last update 2023-04-25, estimated primary completion 2025-05, 132 planned, no results. Europe PMC by number: two reviews (2020, 2022) only; by investigator (Kong B) with sex cord or granulosa in the title: a retrospective series and a review, no trial report. OpenAlex and Crossref title scans (sex cord-stromal, granulosa, with paclitaxel, carboplatin or BEP, 2019-2026, which reach ASCO, ESMO, SGO and IGCS supplements): no report of this trial. One web search in Chinese: registry mirrors only. Not this trial: NRG/GOG-0264 (NCT01042522), a randomised phase 2 of the same comparison (seen in the web search summary only), and Turkish retrospective comparisons of 2026 (titles only). Chinese-language journals and domestic meetings could not be searched, hence medium. Design may be non-inferiority; the record does not say.

which_endpoint: OS: R1 idarubicin vs daunorubicin (superiority) and R2 intermediate- vs high-dose cytarabine (non-inferiority)
search_notes: BIG-1, a phase 2/3 trial with several randomisations and three registered primary outcomes (OS for R1 and R2; acute GVHD for R3; DFS for the nested R4 add-on comparisons). Recorded here: the first disclosure of the R1 and R2 overall survival analyses, ASH 2023 abstract 967 (Blood 142 Suppl 1; text read through OpenAlex and Crossref; date is the supplement issue date in Crossref, the record itself was created 2023-12-01; the abstract does not print the registry number, the NEJM Evidence paper of the same analysis does). R1 (1,159 patients, superiority): idarubicin did not prolong OS, adjusted HR 1.04 (95% CI 0.88-1.23), p=0.67 - not met; this is the HR in the cells. R2 (1,221 patients, non-inferiority margin HR 1.25, per protocol): intermediate dose non-inferior, adjusted p=0.004, no HR in the abstract - met; HR 0.96 (0.80-1.15) first in NEJM Evid 2025-06-24 (PMID 40552969). Hence 'mixed'; if only one sufficient endpoint is wanted it would be 'met' on the non-inferiority comparison. EARLIER disclosure of another registered primary outcome: R4 vosaroxin (18-month leukaemia-free survival, phase 2 stage) at ASH 2020 (DOI 10.1182/blood-2020-137032, Crossref record created 2020-11-04): primary endpoint not met, phase 3 part not opened. Later: R3 MMF GVHD prophylaxis, ASH 2024 (blood-2024-203964), not met (SHR 0.64, 0.35-1.17), names NCT02416388; R1 again and R4 dexamethasone (RFS HR 0.94, not met) at ASH 2025. The registry's 'actual' primary completion date of 2025-07-30 is 21 months after the main disclosure; the record still says recruiting. No web search.

FAVORE (neoadjuvant FOLFOXIRI alone vs capecitabine chemoradiotherapy, rectal cancer; 3-year DFS; 776 planned). Nothing found. Registry never updated since 2019-01-23 (recruiting, estimated primary completion 2025-09-25, no results). Europe PMC by number: one review (Nat Rev Gastroenterol Hepatol, Mar 2024) citing it; by title FOLFOXIRI + rectal with a Sun Yat-sen affiliation or investigator Xu RH: only a 2022 phase 2 report; Crossref title scan of FOLFOXIRI + rectal, 2022-2026, including the JCO and Annals of Oncology supplements: single-arm or other groups' trials only (MEND-IT, SHORT-FOX, ShorTrip, NCT03997435). One web search in Chinese: registry mirrors only. Possibly a non-inferiority design; the record does not say. Weakest of the high rows: the record is stale and the estimated date is a year past.

NRG-GY020 (radiation with or without pembrolizumab, dMMR high-intermediate risk endometrial cancer; 3-year RFS). No result found. Registry: active, not recruiting, 164 enrolled, primary completion 2025-12-30 (actual), no results posted, last update 2026-07-02. NRG Oncology protocol page (opened): accrual closed 2022-08-29, status 'Complete' 2025-12-30, no publications listed. Europe PMC: 36 papers cite the number, 10 from Apr 2025 on mention GY020; in the 8 whose full text opened (latest June 2026) a scripted check found no passage near the trial's name that reports a result, and the passages I read (five papers, to May 2026) call it ongoing or awaited; an Oct 2026 Viewpoint abstract (OpenAlex) still lists it as ongoing. Crossref title scans of pembrolizumab or mismatch repair with endometrial in Gynecologic Oncology (SGO 2025 and 2026 supplements), JCO supplements (ASCO 2025, 2026), IJGC and IJROBP from Feb 2025: no GY020 result. Two web searches: registry and trial-listing pages only. Not this trial: KEYNOTE-B21 (dMMR subgroup) and the D-RT dostarlimab study.

FSRT-Trial (Erlangen; fractionated stereotactic radiotherapy vs single-session radiosurgery; time to local progression). Nothing found. Registry: status unknown, last update 2022-12-13, estimated primary completion 2026-05, 382 planned, no results. Europe PMC by number: six papers; a review of 2026-04-23 (full text opened) lists it among ongoing SRS vs FSRT trials and a 2024 paper says it is recruiting. By investigator (Putz F) with radiosurgery or stereotactic in the title, 2022-2026: no trial report. OpenAlex title and abstract searches: nothing. No web search.

BCTOP-T-M01 (BP102, a bevacizumab biosimilar, plus chemotherapy vs chemotherapy, BLIS-subtype TNBC, first line; PFS). Not read out. Registry updated 2026-03-25: still recruiting, estimated primary completion 2026-05-01, 134 planned, no results. Europe PMC by number: eight reviews; those of Oct 2025, June 2026 and July 2026 (full text opened) list it as ongoing or recruiting. OpenAlex by BP102, BCTOP-T and basal-like immune-suppressed: no result abstract. Not this trial: BCTOP-T-A01 (adjuvant, BMJ 2024) and ASCO 2026 abstract 1020 on bevacizumab with antibody-drug conjugates in BLIS disease (title only). No web search.

COG ASCT2031 (haploidentical vs matched unrelated donor transplant). Not read out. Registry updated 2026-07-30: active, not recruiting, 66 enrolled (actual), primary completion 2026-06-30 (actual), no results, no reason for stopping given. The two primary outcomes (severe GVHD and DFS at 1 year) are worded as estimates of cumulative incidence in each arm, not as a comparison. Europe PMC by number and study ID: only papers that mention the trial in passing (ATG dosing, total body irradiation methods, a COG blueprint). OpenAlex: nothing. One web search: site listing pages only, no closure notice and no results. Whether accrual closed early is not stated anywhere I could open.

GP vs PF induction chemotherapy with CCRT, nasopharyngeal carcinoma (Sun Yat-sen, investigator Ming-Yuan Chen; 3-year PFS). Not read out. Registry: active, not recruiting, last update 2025-01-13, estimated primary completion 2026-08-31, 468 planned, no results. Europe PMC by number and by study ID 2018-FXY-140: no hits; by investigator (Chen MY) with nasopharyngeal and gemcitabine in the title, 2023-2026: a phase 2 in recurrent disease only. OpenAlex and Crossref title scans (gemcitabine + nasopharyngeal + fluorouracil or PF or randomised, 2021-2026, including the JCO and Annals of Oncology supplements): no report of this trial. Not this trial: the adjuvant GP vs PF trial in N2-3 disease (Lancet Oncol 2023, ASCO 2023 abstract 6000; titles only). Two active regimens; the record states no hypothesis. No web search.
